title: What is known about 1RB0RB_1LC1RA_0LF0LD_1LE1RB_1RA1LC_---1LA
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0RB_1LC1RA_0LF0LD_1LE1RB_1RA1LC_---1LA.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. Lean proves the left-going pass and its four endings for every block length (shift, stop at a singleton, halt at a leftmost singleton, or a new leftmost cell) and the counter configuration at step 29,479; a hand argument from the table shows that a halt needs the pass to meet a leftmost block of length 1, given the observed fact that inside the tape 0s are single. Whether that ever happens is not known.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 31,816 cells have been visited and 26,482 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: fixed/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.49).

claims.title: The halting patterns
claims.text: 0 0 E> 1 and 0 A> 1 0 halt (F reads 0); by the table these are the only ways, and the second cannot occur after the start.

claims.title: The pass and its endings
claims.text: The left pass over a block (c_run), and at a separator: a block of length ≥ 2 is shifted right and the pass goes on (c_shift); a block of length 1 stops it (c_stop); a leftmost block of length 1 halts (c_halt); a longer leftmost block gives a new leftmost cell (c_lead). For all lengths and every surrounding tape.

claims.title: The counter at step 29,479
claims.text: After 29,479 steps the tape is Q (110101)^26 1 1 with the head in state A on its last cell (Q a fixed 40-cell prefix).

claims.title: No halt in 1.3·10<sup>11</sup> steps; the depth front
claims.text: The macro simulator finds no halt and no new leftmost cell after step 29,281; the deepest pass moved from 162 to 88 cells from the left end (at 1.3·10<sup>11</sup> steps), each step deeper taking several times as long.

claims.title: Halting needs the left end
claims.text: At every excursion start in the first 2·10<sup>6</sup> steps the 0s inside the tape are single, so the halting pattern can only form at the leftmost block.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known: it halts iff some pass reaches the leftmost block while that block has length 1. The leftmost block is now 1^4; nothing known prevents it from shrinking.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. Each time the head comes back from the right end it pushes the blocks of 1s one cell to the right until it hits a block of length 1. The machine stops only if that block is the very first one on the tape. Lean proves how the pass works; whether a pass ever meets a lone first block is open.

facts.text: The only way to halt: a pass meets a leftmost block of length 1.
The counter on the tape at step 29,479, proved in Lean.
No halt; the deepest pass is 86 cells from the left end.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.49).
After 109 steps the tape spans 31,816 cells (17 left of the start, 23,346 right), with a density of 1s of 0.832.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: The pass
html: The tape is a row of blocks of 1s with single 0s between them. Each time the head comes back from the right end it walks left in states C, B, D, three steps per cell, and at each separator it looks at the block to its left:

block to the leftwhat happenstheorem
length ≥ 2shifted one cell right; the pass goes onc_shift
length 1becomes 1 1; the head turns aroundc_stop
length 1, first on the tapeF reads 0: haltc_halt
first on the tape, longerthe head turns; the tape grows on the leftc_lead
Then it sweeps back right, flipping pairs 11 ↔ 01. All of these are Lean theorems for every block length and every tape around them.

sections.heading: Where it could halt
html: The only halting transition is F on 0. Following the table backwards, F on 0 needs C on 0 just before, which needs E on 1 with 0 0 to its left (A on 1 0 after a 0 cannot happen after the start), and E comes only from D on 0. So a halt is exactly D on a separator with a block of length 1 to its left and two 0s left of that. Inside the tape the 0s are single, so this is the pass meeting the first block of the tape while it has length 1.

sections.heading: A counter that creeps left
html: At step 29,479 the tape is a fixed 40-cell prefix and 26 copies of 110101 (proved in Lean, counter_start). Since each copy holds blocks of length 1, most passes stop near the right end; their depths follow a ruler-like pattern, and the deepest so far moves left slowly:

When the front reaches the prefix, the question is what the first block looks like then. It is 1^4 now, and passes that stop at the second block rewrite its end. Starting from shorter counters (m copies instead of 26, m = 0 … 9 and 11) the front reaches the left end without a halt every time, after a number of excursions that grows fast but irregularly with m.

sections.heading: What is proved, and what is not
html: Proved in Lean by the kernel: the halting patterns, the pass and its four endings. With native_decide: the counter at step 29,479. Measured with a simulator: no halt in 1.3·1011 steps, the depth records, the small-counter runs. Not proved: that the 0s inside the tape stay single (so that halting needs the left end), a macro step on the block word, and anything about the first block when the front arrives.

family: Block-shifting counter: a pass stops at the first block of length 1; halting needs a leftmost singleton
summary: Every excursion sends a pass left that shifts blocks of 1s one cell right until it meets a block of length 1; the machine halts only if the pass reaches the leftmost block when it has length 1. The deepest passes creep towards the left end like a counter; no halt in 1.3·10^11 steps.
